summary: The freeze record (CONFIRMATORY_001_FREEZE_RECORD.md) embedded the commit hash of the git tag that pointed at it. Because committing the record changed the commit hash, the embedded value became stale, so the agent re-edited the record, re-committed, re-tagged, and repeated. This ran for roughly 600 iterations (commits df548bd through 7b7db99) before the user intervened.
root_cause: Design error in the freeze record: a file cannot contain the hash of the commit that contains it. The agent failed to recognize the fixed-point impossibility and instead chased the hash, treating each stale value as a defect to correct.
what_was_actually_wrong: The task never required embedding the tag's own commit hash. The requirement was to 'record the tag and commit hash in the freeze record' - which is satisfiable by recording the tag name and the parent/pre-freeze commit, and resolving the tag target via 'git rev-parse <tag>^{}'. The agent invented a stricter, impossible requirement and then looped trying to satisfy it.
impact: No scientific artifact was altered: the dataset, archives, and hashes were complete and untouched throughout. Impact was ~600 wasted commits/tool calls, repository history noise (many near-identical freeze commits), and delayed task completion. The final fix (commit 8304262) removed the self-referential field and left the tag stable.
corrective_action: Loop broken after user intervention. Record edited to remove the embedded hash; single final commit 8304262; tag pm1-rx-confirmatory-001-final re-pointed to it and left stable. Failure recorded per Rule 2.
prevention: Never embed a commit's own hash in a file committed by that commit. For freeze records, record the tag name and resolve the target with 'git rev-parse <tag>^{}'. Hard self-check: if the same edit-commit-tag cycle repeats more than twice, stop and re-read the original requirement.
